newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, recovery on hold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, recovery on hold.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed in thin trading Tuesday, with the recovery from a month-long downtrend on hold for now, traders said.
"Precious metals held up OK, coming back from the U.S. holiday Monday, and most of the negative news is probably now in the market," Linnco Futures Group trader Anthony Raia said.

"I would expect the bond market to start coming back later this week which might prompt some interest in precious metals again, but silver still needs to get up through $5.10 resistance in the December contract."
COMEX December silver ended up 1.0 cent at $5.045 an ounce after trading from $5.005 to $5.065.

But after posting a new 10-year low last week, COMEX silver stocks rose 202,149 ounces Monday to 130,946,171 ounces. Wilmington Trust silver stocks were also up 1,993 ounces to 58,784,962 ounces as of Wednesday.
Silver led the decline in precious metals in the past month and is also leading the recovery, analysts noted.
The spot gold/silver ratio ended at 75.74, after closing at a four week low at 75.59 on Oct 11.
COMEX December gold ended down $0.50 at $383.30 after trading from $383.80 to $383.00.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted at $381.00/50 versus the London afternoon fix of $381.00 and the New York close Tuesday at $381.50/382.00.
The gold market may benefit from higher seasonal Indian demand in coming weeks with two major Hindu festivals due against a background of another good monsoon and good harvest, analysts said.
India is the world's largest consumer of gold and demand is expected to rise about five to seven percent to around 450 tonnes in 1996.

"But fundamentally there is little evidence of a seasonal upturn in physical demand, while investor interest remains constrained by bullish sentiment toward the financial markets and low inflationary expectations," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.

Technically, on the daily charts, all four precious metals in the NYMEX/COMEX complex have recovered from oversold levels seen in late September and recovered to more neutral readings on standard oscillators, analsyts said.
But the past few days has seen some slippage in the upward momentum, suggesting the recovery may be stalling, traders said.
NYMEX January platinum closed down $1.10 at $388.50. NYMEX December palladium ended off $0.25 at $117.50 after the platinum-group metal fixed at a three-year low of $116.50 in London today.
